name: Gesher Benot Ya‘aqov inferred fish cooking
description: Researchers interpret heat-altered fish remains associated with burned artifacts as evidence that hominins cooked freshwater fish.

impact.note: One site's inferred evidence of cooking; cooking is a new ability, but nothing is known to descend from this group.

date.label: About 780,000 years ago
date.basis: Approximate reported site age; calendar position is approximate at this resolution.

events.statement: Researchers interpret heat-altered fish remains associated with burned artifacts as evidence that hominins cooked freshwater fish.

evidence.supports: At about 780,000 years ago, fish teeth associated with burned artifacts and heat alteration are interpreted as cooking; the interpretation and temperature reconstruction are indirect.

events.caveats: Cooking and intentional heating are indirect interpretations of an archaeological assemblage; only the university-hosted abstract was accessible. This is not a claim about the global origin of cooking.
